_comment: The sales-report half of the storefront taxonomy. The shelf a product sits on is
declared once, in zz_tp/documents/<listing>/config.tl as `category = "kidney"`, and
that declaration is what the catalogue, the shop's filter chips and the collection
pages all read. Nothing here decides a product's shelf.
What lives here is the other direction: which sales-report keyword family rolls up into
which shelf, so a report and the shop can be read side by side. The families stay
finer than the shelf on purpose - 'diverticulitis outsold gout' is worth keeping, and
it costs nothing to keep above a shelf that both feed.
buckets lists the shelves the shop has, in display order, so a checker can catch a
config.tl that names one the shop does not have, and a docs page that names one the
config never uses. The labels live in src/realkevbase-web/src/data/hubLinks.ts; the two
lists are asserted equal rather than copied.
The four Etsy-era categories (healthy-living, money-budgeting, moving-out, guides) are
deliberately absent. They were the sales report's groupings, and 'guides' was the
fallback for a family the report did not recognise, not a subject.

unmappedFamilies.reason: No wedding product exists or is planned; the family stays in the sales rules so historical rows still group, but it has no shelf to roll into.
families.py's own catch-all: a title that matched no keyword. A shelf for it would be the 'guides' mistake again.
